items.title: Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2022
items.q: one of the pieces like “Gates of Justice” is a combination of Old Testament, New Testament, and Martin Luther King.

ctx.x: I’ve had the privilege of being in the Brubeck house twice to interview your parents. And I was struck, Dave had been working on a piece the day I got there and he took me to the piano and he said come on. It was for piano and voice, and the war in Afghanistan had just started and it was reflective of that. And it was interesting because he said, “Iola said no one will want to sing it. It’s too sad.” And I got this little picture of their back and forth and her opinions, voicing her opinions about his music, in…

Yeah well she was deeply involved in the evolution of all the religious pieces he wrote and there’s like 17 or 18 of them where a lot of it would be Bible quotes but you know one of the pieces like “Gates of Justice” is a combination of Old Testament, New Testament, and Martin Luther King. And Dan and I both know that you know like there are so many misconceptions about my dad but one of them is that he wrote all this music that had Biblical text and you might conclude oh he’s Jimmy Swaggart that plays jazz piano…
He came to Catholicism fairly late in life, didn’t he? I think I read something where someone asked him about it and he said well I didn’t come from anything. I don’t know if he was an agnostic.
